tutorial.title: Python Modules
tutorial.descriptionContent: Transfer module, multi-file program, and package skills through interleaved challenges.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who want harder practice after tutorials 4600-4602

lessons.title: Redesign the Exhibit Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
A museum app needs exhibit lookup and admission calculations. Which design keeps the modules focused?

exhibits.py handles exhibit lookup, and admissions.py handles admission calculationsmuseum.py handles exhibits, admissions, accounts, and emailtools.py stores every unrelated helperscript.py is the only Python file used

exhibits.py handles exhibit lookup, and admissions.py handles admission calculations.

Why does Demo exhibit appear before Open?

lessons.title: Classify Analytics Modules
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which statement stays true for project, standard-library, and installed modules?

The same import forms work when Python can find the named moduleInstalled modules use a different import keywordStandard-library imports must name Python as the authorProject modules cannot use selective imports

The same import forms work when Python can find the named module.

lessons.title: Predict the Guarded Run
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when script.py imports this guarded module?

The demo stays quiet because __name__ is exhibit_toolsThe demo runs because __name__ is __main__Python skips every function definitionThe import changes __name__ inside script.py

The demo stays quiet because __name__ is exhibit_tools.

lessons.title: Check Module Findability
lessons.interactiveContent:
A project module, math, and an installed module all use normal imports. What determines whether each import succeeds?

Python can find the module in the project, standard library, or active environmentThe import statement lists who wrote itEvery module lives in the current folderOnly standard-library modules can use import

Python can find the module in the project, standard library, or active environment.
